newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end little changed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end little changed.

text.p: Swiss shares closed little changed on Tuesday in fairly active trade and dealers said the market was likely to move sideways during the next few sessions.
Banks recouped some of the earlier losses and dealers said the sector seemed to have bottomed out.

The banks had come under pressure from reports of threats by Jewish groups to call a boycott of Swiss banking institutions because of Switzerland's handling of the issue of dormant assets of Holocaust victims.
The broad SPI closed 4.41 points higher at 2,510.63, but the blue-chip SMI was down 0.9 to 3,922.9.
Novartis, down three to 1,522, led the actives list.
Most blue chips closed easier as many investors turned to second-tier shares for higher yields.
UBS rose nine francs to 1,158. CS Group was steady at 133.75. SBC lost two to close at 250.50.
Dealers said there were renewed interest rate worries in the market with some investors awaiting Friday's U.S. employment for a signal on rates.
Rate worries also put some pressure on insurers. Swiss Re fell 11 to 1,432.
The second-tier sector saw OZ Holding 53 francs higher at 602. Kuoni added 105 to end at 3,525.
